Memorised in the G9 الإلقاء وحدة and used in every delivery thereafter.

classicalTexts.title: خطبة حجة الوداع
classicalTexts.justification: Transmitted in the hadith collections and in سيرة ابن هشام. Used at G10 as the first worked example of a complete address with a clear مقدمة، عرض، خاتمة. Analysed for structure; the student is not asked to reproduce it. Coordinate with السيرة والتاريخ الإسلامي so it is studied once, from two angles, not taught twice.

classicalTexts.title: صبح الأعشى في صناعة الإنشا — القلقشندي
classicalTexts.grade: Teacher reference only; not a student text at any grade
classicalTexts.justification: A chancery manual of many volumes on the craft of official composition. Genuinely the classical reference on صناعة الإنشاء, and useful to a specialist teacher building letter and report conventions, but wholly unsuitable as a taught text in a 12-year school. Listed so the board knows the tradition has a canonical reference here and that I am deliberately not putting it in front of students.

classicalTexts.title: مقامات الحريري
classicalTexts.grade: NOT RECOMMENDED for this subject at any grade
classicalTexts.justification: The work certainly exists and is classically used in أدب teaching, but I am recommending against it here on discipline grounds, not availability grounds. Its ornate saj' and lexical display teach exactly the opposite of what an L2 composition programme needs — it models showing off vocabulary rather than communicating clearly. If the board wants it, it belongs to النقد والآداب as an object of literary study, never to الإنشاء as a model for imitation.

classicalTexts.title: نهج البلاغة — جمع الشريف الرضي
classicalTexts.grade: [COUNCIL DECISION REQUIRED] — not adopted by me
classicalTexts.justification: The collection exists and is famous precisely as a body of Arabic oratory. I am not placing it in the ladder. Its compilation history and the attribution of its contents are contested, and in a Sunni Nigerian institution its adoption is a governance question with communal implications, not a pedagogical one I may settle alone. Flagged rather than silently used or silently dropped.

classicalTexts.title: جواهر الأدب — أحمد الهاشمي
classicalTexts.grade: [UNVERIFIED as to exact title] — do not adopt until a physical copy is checked
classicalTexts.justification: I am confident أحمد الهاشمي (d. 1943) is a real author of widely used Arabic language manuals including جواهر البلاغة. I am NOT sufficiently confident of the exact title and subtitle of a companion work on إنشاء to let the board build on it. Per the hard prohibition, I am naming my uncertainty rather than asserting the text. If a copy is verified it would suit G10-G12 as a teacher-side resource.

classicalTexts.title: No classical matn for G1-G9
classicalTexts.justification: This is a positive finding, not a gap. Classical Arabic pedagogy did not teach إنشاء from a matn; it taught it by imitation (المعارضة), dictation of models, and correction. Composition in an L2 setting must be built from the learner's own life-world and from content already met in الفقه، الحديث، السيرة — not from a memorised treatise. Inserting an impressive-sounding matn into the early years of this subject would repeat exactly the error redline 1 corrected for نخبة الفكر.

lifecycles.lifecycleVerdict: continuous (from G3 to G12, absent G1-G2, with scope that widens rather than narrows — الخطابة joins at G10)
lifecycles.prematureIntroductionRisks: Three specific failures, not one generic one. (1) A composition subject before G6 has no النحو for the learner to self-correct against, so "composition" degenerates into copying a board model and swapping one noun. This trains the single most damaging habit available in Arabic-as-L2 teaching: producing Arabic the learner cannot analyse, vary, or defend. It is the direct ancestor of the graduate who delivers a fluent khutbah and cannot answer a question about a sentence in it. (2) A standalone slot before G8 costs one to two of the 19 periods that النحو والصرف need in order to reach the very competence الإنشاء depends on — the subject would be eating its own prerequisites. At G1-G2 with only 7 periods, any claim at all comes out of القراءة والتهجي and damages decoding, which gates everything. (3) خطابة before G10 is the serious one. An adolescent placed on a minbar earns applause for fluency he does not own, and the applause, not comprehension, becomes the goal; the performance culture then becomes very hard to reverse. Worse, a student speaking in the register of religious authority before he has مصطلح الحديث (G10-G11) will cite hadith he cannot source, and before أدب الخطاب (G12) may pronounce on بدعة or on named individuals in his own community. Given redline 6's concern about نواقض الإسلام at G5, giving a G7 or G8 student a public voice before giving him the ethics of that voice is a live communal risk, not a theoretical one.
lifecycles.delayRisks: Also three, and they are why I override the submission's total omission. (1) If الإنشاء is never given a traceable identity and a separate mark before G8 — that is, if it is left dissolved in اللغة العربية as the submission implicitly leaves it — production is silently dropped. Composition is the slowest thing to mark and the first thing a teacher carrying a 19-period load cuts. Once it carries no separate mark, there is no evidence it was ever taught, and the school discovers at G9 that students with strong النحو results cannot write five connected sentences. This is the most common single failure of Arabic L2 programmes and it is cheap to prevent: the G5 مضمّن + independently assessed decision costs zero periods. (2) The submitted G6 الترجمة (التفسير العملي rendered into English and Yoruba) already assumes productive competence the submitted curriculum never builds. Delaying الإنشاء past G6 leaves الترجمة standing on nothing on the Arabic side. (3) Delaying الخطابة past G10 into G11-G12 compresses it below the practice threshold and, more importantly, misses the window in which the community itself starts asking these students to lead prayer, speak at a naming ceremony, or teach younger children. If the school does not train that voice at G10-G12, the community will train it — informally, unsupervised, and badly.
lifecycles.g12Role: At G12 this is the subject in which the entire twelve-year edifice becomes publicly visible. The graduate can: compose, without a model in front of him, a structured Arabic address of 7-10 minutes with a proper مقدمة، عرض، خاتمة, opened with خطبة الحاجة, evidenced by آيات he has memorised in the ring-fenced Qur'an hour and by hadith he can attribute because of مصطلح الحديث, and deliver it to a real audience with controlled voice and pace; write an 800-1200 word رسالة أو مقالة in correct Arabic on a topic from the Islamic sciences, with sourced evidence and a defensible argument; produce a parallel Yoruba or English rendering of his own address, making him usable in his own community and not only in an Arabic-speaking one; and — the part the board should weigh most heavily — know the limits of the pulpit: he exhorts, teaches and consoles, he does not issue فتوى, he does not pass public judgement on named individuals or families, and he refers what exceeds his competence. Every other subject in the ladder produces a graduate who knows something. This one produces a graduate who can be heard, which is the only form in which the rest of it reaches anyone else.
lifecycles.periodsRequested: G1-G2 (7/wk ceiling): ZERO periods. Explicitly and deliberately no claim. G3-G4 (19/wk): ZERO additional periods — roughly 15 minutes of oral-production work per week drawn from the اللغة العربية block, named in the scheme, embedded in its assessment. G5 (19/wk): ZERO additional periods — same arrangement, but with a separately reported mark. The mark costs nothing; only the marking time costs anything. G6-G7 (19/wk): ONE period per week, ring-fenced INSIDE the existing اللغة العربية allocation, not added to it. اللغة العربية's block is split internally; the total number of timetabled subjects is unchanged. G8-G9 (19/wk): ONE period per week, newly claimed. This is the subject's first real draw on the ceiling, at grade 8 of 12 — a modest claim by the standards of the register. G10-G12 (19/wk): TWO periods per week (one composition, one delivery workshop), which is the whole claim for the compound subject الإنشاء والخطابة. Two periods is sufficient only because the termly PUBLIC delivery uses assembly time, which the school already spends, rather than a timetable period. If the board will not release assembly time, this subject needs three periods at G10-G12 and I would rather the board know that now than discover it in year one. Total lifetime claim against the 19-period ceiling: 0 at G1-G5, 0 net at G6-G7, 1 at G8-G9, 2 at G10-G12.
relationshipToOtherSubjects: FED BY اللغة العربية — its host and its parent from G3 to G7. الإنشاء is the productive counterpart of الإملاء, which redline 7 correctly keeps longitudinal inside اللغة العربية; the same logic governs الإنشاء in the early years, and I apply it deliberately rather than by analogy alone.

FED BY النحو (الآجرومية G6, ملحة الإعراب G7) and الصرف (البناء G6, لامية الأفعال G7). MUST NOT DUPLICATE them: الإنشاء never teaches إعراب, it enforces it in the learner's own output. Boundary rule — النحو owns the analysis, الإنشاء owns the production and its rubric. This relationship runs both ways: الإنشاء is the output valve that stops الآجرومية producing learners who parse beautifully and write nothing.

FED BY البلاغة from G9 onward. MUST NOT DUPLICATE it: البلاغة owns the terminology (التشبيه، الاستعارة، الكناية، المجاز) and the analysis of canonical lines; الإنشاء consumes that vocabulary in production and never re-teaches the theory. CRITICAL REGISTER WARNING for the board: البلاغة's own technical term الإنشاء (الطلبي وغير الطلبي, opposed to الخبر) is a completely different sense of the word from this subject's الإنشاء = composition. Two entries in the 26-subject register will look like they overlap and do not. Please annotate the register so no future committee merges them.

FED BY النشيد والمحفوظات (G3-G7). This is the unacknowledged bridge: reciting تحفة الأطفال, ديوان الشافعي and تائية الإلبيري before an audience builds the voice, breath control, memorised high register and public poise that الخطابة draws on at G10. Without it, G10 would be starting from silence. Protect النشيد on these grounds as well as its own.

FED BY the ring-fenced Qur'an hour, at zero cost. حفظ supplies the citation bank without which composition and خطابة become assertion. This is the clearest case in the whole architecture of the constitutional Qur'an hour paying dividends into another programme.
FED BY الفقه، الحديث، السيرة، العقيدة — the content base. Composition without subject matter becomes ornament, which is precisely how إنشاء teaching fails when it is run as a pure language exercise.

FED BY مصطلح الحديث (G10-G11, per redline 1). Enables the rule this subject enforces from G11: no hadith is cited in writing or from the minbar unless the student can name its source. This is a concrete, checkable payoff of the redline board's decision to move نخبة الفكر to G10-G11.

FEEDS الترجمة (from G6). Under-recognised dependency: rendering out of Arabic is receptive, but rendering INTO Arabic is composition. The submitted G6 التفسير العملي + الترجمة assumes an Arabic productive capacity the submission does not build anywhere — this subject must be present at G6 for that submitted allocation to stand up. At G12 the relationship reverses and الترجمة enables the Yoruba/English rendering of the student's own خطبة.

FEEDS النقد والآداب. A student cannot judge a text finely until he has tried to make one; production should lead criticism, not follow it. Sequencing implication for that specialist: النقد is better placed at or after G10, not before.
FEEDS أصول الفقه indirectly — structured argument, claim-and-evidence, and the discipline of qualification are the same habits in both, though the content is entirely separate.

FEEDS التربية الإسلامية and the school's دعوة function. MUST NOT DUPLICATE it: الخطابة owns the craft of address — structure, evidence, delivery, ethics of the pulpit — and must never become a second وعظ class supplying doctrinal content that other subjects already own.
FEEDS الدراسات الحديثة: report and essay structure transfers directly, and this is the one place the two programmes' written conventions can be made to agree rather than compete.
MARGINAL relationship to العروض — rhythm awareness sharpens prose cadence, but I claim nothing from it and it should not be sequenced around this subject.
departuresFromSubmission: OVERRIDE at G5-G7: the submission omits this subject entirely from G1-G7. For G5, G6 and G7 that omission is wrong and I am reversing it. Not by adding a timetable subject — by requiring that التعبير be a named, separately marked outcome inside the existing اللغة العربية allocation from G5, and a مدمج strand with one ring-fenced period from G6. The cost is zero new periods. The cost of NOT doing it is a G8 cohort with good النحو marks that cannot produce connected Arabic, which is the most common and least visible failure mode in this kind of programme.

PROTECT at G1-G4: the submission's omission here is CORRECT and I am explicitly endorsing it, not correcting it. At 7 periods per week and الحروف/المفردات level there is nothing to compose with, and any claim damages القراءة والتهجي. G3-G4 oral production is real but it belongs to اللغة العربية's own teaching and I claim only a مضمّن, embedded-assessment presence there. I raise this because a board reviewing 26 subjects will feel pressure to make every subject appear early; I am declining that pressure for four grades.

OVERRIDE the register's naming: 'الإنشاء والخطابة' as a single compound entity is only accurate from G10. From G3 to G9 only the الإنشاء half exists, and from G3 to G7 it does not exist as a subject at all. Treating the register entry as one thing with one lifecycle would force الخطابة down into grades where it does damage, or hold الإنشاء up out of grades where it is needed. The two halves have genuinely different lifecycles and the board should record them as such.

IDENTIFY a gap in the submitted G6: the submitted الترجمة إلى الإنجليزية واليوربا at G6 presupposes an Arabic productive competence that no submitted subject builds. This is not a criticism of the الترجمة decision, which is sound and is protected by redline 8 — it is a missing prerequisite that my G6 مدمج allocation supplies at no extra cost.

DECLINE to claim the G10-G12 public delivery as timetable time: I am deliberately routing the خطابة practicum through existing assembly time rather than requesting a third period. The board should treat this as a conditional allocation, not a free one — if assembly time is not released, the request rises to three periods at G10-G12.
openQuestions: [COUNCIL DECISION REQUIRED] At which grade does البلاغة differentiate? My G10 خطابة differentiation assumes البلاغة foundations (التشبيه، الاستعارة، الكناية، مطابقة الكلام لمقتضى الحال) are live by G9. If the البلاغة specialist places it at G10 or later, either خطابة slips to G11 — which pushes it below the practice-cycle threshold — or it proceeds on a thinner rhetorical base. This is the single hardest external dependency in my design and the two specialists should be made to agree before either allocation is ratified.

[COUNCIL DECISION REQUIRED] Do female students deliver خطابة publicly, and to what audience? This determines the entire practicum design at G10-G12, and in the Nigerian context it is a governance and community question, not a pedagogical one. I will not assume an answer. If the answer is a separate audience, the two practicums need separate assembly slots and the timetable implication must be costed now, not in year one.

[COUNCIL DECISION REQUIRED] Is the G12 public خطبة a graduation requirement or merely a graded component? My recommendation is that it be a requirement — it is the one outcome of this school that the surrounding community can directly witness — but making it a requirement creates a real failure pathway for otherwise strong students and the board must own that decision.

[COUNCIL DECISION REQUIRED] Language of the G12 capstone address: Arabic only, or Arabic with a full parallel Yoruba/English delivery? Community function argues for both; the 19-period ceiling argues for Arabic plus a prepared summary. Needs a joint ruling with the الترجمة specialist.

[COUNCIL DECISION REQUIRED] نهج البلاغة — adopt, exclude, or use selectively? It is genuinely the most famous single body of Arabic oratory, and I have deliberately left it out of my ladder rather than quietly using or quietly dropping it. This belongs to the board, not to me.

[UNVERIFIED] The title I associate with أحمد الهاشمي on إنشاء needs a physical copy checked before anything is built on it. I am confident of the author and of جواهر البلاغة; I am not confident enough of the companion title to name it as settled.

[COUNCIL DECISION REQUIRED] Marking load. Composition portfolios are the most labour-intensive marking in the whole register, and this subject asks for them at eight grades. Two periods a week of teaching can generate six hours a week of marking at G10-G12. The board should rule on class size for this subject specifically, or on a moderated-sample marking policy, before the allocation is treated as affordable.

[COUNCIL DECISION REQUIRED] Teacher capacity. This subject needs a teacher who can both correct Arabic prose and coach delivery. Those are not the same person by default. If only one such teacher exists, the G10-G12 workshop period is the one to staff first.

lifecycles.firstMeaningfulAppearance: G2. "Meaningful" for الإملاء has a precise test: the discipline exists only where the writer faces an ORTHOGRAPHIC CHOICE — a point at which the same sound could be written more than one way, and convention (not phonology) decides. At G1 the child is mapping sound→letter shape and forming letters; there is no choice, therefore no إملاء, only القراءة والتهجي and letter formation. At G2, once اللغة العربية reaches الحروف والمفردات and the child writes a connected WORD, the first genuine orthographic choices appear: which of the three positional forms of the letter (مبتدئة / متوسطة / متطرفة) is correct here; which six letters refuse to connect forward (ا د ذ ر ز و) so the word looks "broken" but is one word; ل+ا = لا; where the space between words falls when و / ف / ب / ك / ل / ال are prefixed. That is الإملاء المنقول and it is real learning. [PROFESSIONAL INFERENCE]. Naming anything at G1 "إملاء" would be a mislabel that invites premature rule-teaching and would claim time from a 7-period week.

gradeByGrade.content: Not taught as a distinct entity. What happens this year belongs to القراءة والتهجي and to letter formation: sound→letter correspondence, the three positional shapes of each letter, tracing and copying single letters, direction of stroke. No orthographic choice exists at letter level, so there is nothing for الإملاء to govern. Deliberately '—' and not مضمّن: a phantom entry here would invite rule-teaching (همزة وصل/قطع, تاء مربوطة) a year before the child can write a word, and would put pressure on a 7-period week.

الإملاء المنقول (copy from a model in view). Content: writing a fully-vowelled 3–4 letter word from a model; correct selection of positional letter form; the six non-connecting letters (ا د ذ ر ز و) and the resulting internal gap that is NOT a word break; ل+ا = لا; word spacing; sitting on the line. Taught in the closing 8–10 minutes of existing القراءة والتهجي lessons — transcription is the write-side mirror of the decoding this strand already teaches. No rules stated, only correct models copied.

الإملاء المنظور (look at a short vowelled word/phrase, cover it, write it). Content: writing الحركات الثلاث والسكون والشدة accurately; كتابة التنوين, especially تنوين الفتح on the supporting alif (كتابًا, هدًى); اللام الشمسية والقمرية as a WRITING fact — ال is always written even when not pronounced (الشمس, not اششمس); distinguishing ة from ه at word end by the صلة test (say the word with a following vowel: مدرسةٌ vs وجهُهُ). Word-boundary work with the prefixes و ف ب ك ل. Still no exception lists.

إملاء منظور extended to the short sentences اللغة العربية now teaches (المفردات والجمل القصيرة). Content: a closed, memorised high-frequency list rather than any rule — حذف الألف in هذا، هذه، ذلك، لكن، الرحمن، طه، إله; ابن / اسم written without همزة قطع; و of عمرو; ألف مائة. These are chosen precisely because they are the words a Qur'an-memorising child writes daily. Also begun: transcription of short مَحفوظات the child already knows by heart, so memory carries the wording and attention is free for the orthography. G4 already carries تحفة الأطفال — الإملاء adds no mark and no period this year.

DIFFERENTIATION YEAR. الإملاء becomes a named strand with its own published rule syllabus and its own mark, still with no timetable slot. Content, now rule-governed because الصرف has arrived مضمّن this year: همزة الوصل والقطع (ال التعريف; the سماعية nouns اسم، ابن، ابنة، امرؤ، امرأة، اثنان، اثنتان; أمر الثلاثي vs ماضي وأمر ومصدر الخماسي والسداسي); الألف اللينة في آخر الكلمة — الثلاثي referred back to its root (دعا/يدعو بالألف، رمى/يرمي بالياء، عصا، فتى) and فوق الثلاثي written ى unless preceded by ياء (أعطى، مستشفى، but دنيا، استحيا); التاء المفتوحة والمربوطة والهاء systematically. One weekly 10–15 minute قطعة إملاء with a correction-and-rewrite cycle (the rewrite, not the red ink, is the teaching).

gradeByGrade.partner: الصرف (متن البناء في الصرف), inside اللغة العربية
gradeByGrade.content: الهمزة المتوسطة — the largest and most systematic block in Arabic orthography — placed here because البناء في الصرف gives the وزن and حركة awareness the rule needs. Content: ranking الحركات (الكسرة > الضمة > الفتحة > السكون); comparing the hamza's own حركة with the حركة of the letter before it; writing it على الياء (سُئِل، بِئْر)، على الواو (مُؤمن، سُؤال)، على الألف (سَأَل، يَأْمُر)، على السطر (قراءة، مروءة). Also, and specific to this school: contrastive guard for the year الترجمة begins — English/Yoruba romanisation habits must not leak back into Arabic spelling, and the Yoruba phoneme inventory has no ع ح ق غ ص ض ط ظ ذ ث contrasts, so every mis-heard phoneme becomes a mis-spelled letter. G6 is the heaviest submitted year: zero new periods, taught in the closure of الصرف lessons.

gradeByGrade.partner: الصرف (متن لامية الأفعال), inside اللغة العربية
gradeByGrade.content: الهمزة المتطرفة, riding on the الإعلال والإبدال that لامية الأفعال handles — the very processes that move hamza and alif. Content: final hamza written according to the حركة of the letter before it (قرَأ، لؤلؤ، شاطئ، دِفْء، جزء); final hamza after a ساكن written على السطر; and the notorious hamza + تنوين الفتح set (جزءًا، شيئًا، عبئًا، بطيئًا، ماءً). MILESTONE: by the end of G7 the entire رسم إملائي rule-set has been DELIVERED. Everything after this grade is application, not new rules — which is why the mark converts at G8.

gradeByGrade.partner: اللغة العربية + الإنشاء والخطابة (wherever the Council places it; recommended G8)
gradeByGrade.content: Function changes from learning rules to holding a standard under composition load. Content: الوصل والفصل (مما، عمّا، ألّا، لئلا، حينئذٍ، كأنما); علامات الترقيم taught as a system, not as decoration (الفاصلة، الفاصلة المنقوطة، النقطة، علامتا التنصيص، الشرطة، علامة الاستفهام); and the shift from writing fully-vowelled text to writing شبه مجرد text, keeping تشكيل only where ambiguity demands it. التصحيح الذاتي protocol: the student proof-reads his own composition against a named checklist before submission. Assessment converts to embedded plus a school-wide error-tolerance threshold applied to written work in EVERY subject — because the question is no longer 'does he know the rule' but 'does he apply it while thinking about something else', which only real writing can measure.

gradeByGrade.text: قواعد الإملاء لعبد السلام محمد هارون (student reference, modern)
gradeByGrade.content: Sustained unvowelled connected prose. Content: quotation and citation conventions a student of this school actually needs — Qur'anic آيات set within ﴿ ﴾ and NEVER re-spelled into الرسم الإملائي inside them; hadith quoted with «» and followed by تخريج (رواه البخاري، أخرجه مسلم); كتابة الأرقام والتواريخ الهجرية والميلادية; correct writing of أسماء الأعلام والكنى (أبو / أبي / أبا, عمرو vs عمر, ابن at the start of a line vs between two names). Feeds الحديث, السيرة والتاريخ الإسلامي and any written الفقه answer.

gradeByGrade.text: المقنع في رسم مصاحف الأمصار لأبي عمرو الداني (teacher reference and selected extracts)
gradeByGrade.content: A bounded short course of roughly 8–10 periods in ONE term, hosted inside اللغة العربية's existing allocation, on الفرق بين الرسم الإملائي والرسم العثماني: why الصلوة، الزكوة، الرحمن، أولئك، بأييد، لأاذبحنه are written as they are in the مصحف; that رسم عثماني is a transmitted convention (سنة متبعة in the view of the majority) and not a spelling option; and the practical editorial ruling — Qur'an quoted as Qur'an is written in الرسم العثماني, the same words used as ordinary Arabic vocabulary are written in الرسم الإملائي. This is the one point in twelve years where إملاء takes a distinct bounded shape of its own. It is a وحدة and not a permanent slot because it is a finite body of knowledge, not a skill needing distributed practice.

gradeByGrade.partner: across all written work (الإنشاء والخطابة، البلاغة، النقد والآداب، أصول الفقه essays)
gradeByGrade.text: قواعد الإملاء لعبد السلام هارون (reference); عقيلة أتراب القصائد للشاطبي — optional, Ijazah/higher track only
gradeByGrade.content: Editorial standard, no teaching block. Content added this year is narrow and real: reading and transcribing from older printings and photographed manuscripts, where hamza conventions differ from the modern standard (شئ / شيء, مسئول / مسؤول, هؤلاء spellings), and where تشكيل is partial or absent. The student learns to normalise an old text into modern رسم إملائي when quoting it, and to say when he has done so. Serves anyone who will handle primary sources — which, in this school, is everyone by G12.

No teaching entity remains; a graduation threshold does. Every piece of the G12 written output — the بحث, the مقال, the خطبة script — is held to a published orthographic standard, and a failure to meet it is returned for correction rather than absorbed into a content mark. The one new competence is other-directed: the student proof-reads a peer's Arabic text and marks it accurately. This is also where the school's international ambition is cashed: an application, a scholarship essay or an entrance paper going to an Arabic-medium institution must not be discounted on hamza errors before its content is read.

lifecycles.differentiationPoint: Two distinct answers, and they must not be confused. (1) الإملاء NEVER becomes مستقل — it never takes a timetable line, at any of the twelve grades. I affirm redline 7 on the discipline's own grounds, not merely as compliance: إملاء is a performance skill with a small closed rule-set and a large practice requirement; a weekly standalone period would divorce spelling from the composition where transfer must happen, and would reproduce the classic failure of scoring 9/10 on Friday's dictation and misspelling the same words in Monday's إنشاء. It would also cost 1 of only 19 periods permanently. [CURRENT COUNCIL DIRECTION] + [PROFESSIONAL INFERENCE]. (2) It DOES differentiate at G5 into a named, separately-marked strand with a published rule syllabus — which is a different thing from a subject, and this distinction is the whole engineering of this submission. Why G5 and not G4: the rule-governed core of الإملاء is parasitic on الصرف. همزة الوصل والقطع is decidable only by knowing أمر الثلاثي from the خماسي والسداسي; الألف اللينة is decidable only by returning the ثلاثي to its واوي/يائي root. الصرف first appears in this curriculum مضمّن at G5. Teach these at G4 and they can only be delivered as arbitrary word-lists the child must guess at — which is worse than not teaching them, because guessing fossilises. Why G5 and not G6: two reasons. First, G6 is by far the heaviest submitted year (الآجرومية، البناء في الصرف، الجزرية، الأخضري، التفسير العملي مع الترجمة) and cannot absorb a new named strand. Second, and decisively, G4–G5 is exactly when free written output begins in volume; a year of unmarked, unnamed spelling is a year of rehearsed error, and Arabic hamza errors laid down in that window are among the most persistent literacy faults into adulthood. [NEW ENGINEERING DECISION]. (3) A separate, bounded differentiation at G10 as a وحدة on الرسم العثماني — see G10.
prerequisites: Sound→letter correspondence and command of all three positional forms of every letter — established G1 in القراءة والتهجي, secure by end of G2. Without it there is no writing at all, only drawing.
Grapho-motor control sufficient to write a connected word legibly at speed — G2. If handwriting is still effortful, all attention goes to the hand and none to the orthography.

Accurate reading of a fully-vowelled word (الحركات الثلاث، السكون، الشدة، التنوين) — G2–G3 via القراءة والتهجي; التنوين secure by G3. إملاء is transcription: you cannot write what you cannot read back.

Phonemic discrimination of the Arabic-specific consonant contrasts ع/ء، ح/ه، ق/ك، غ/خ، ص/س، ض/د، ظ/ذ/ز، ط/ت، ث/س — G1–G3, delivered FREE inside the ring-fenced Qur'an hour by the practical التجويد / مخارج الحروف strand. This is the single most important prerequisite for a Yoruba- and English-speaking intake, because Yoruba's inventory has none of these contrasts: an unheard phoneme becomes a mis-written letter, permanently. [PROFESSIONAL INFERENCE]
الوقف awareness — that ة is realised as ه in pause — needed before ة / ه / ت can be separated. Available from the practical التجويد strand and from القراءة والتهجي by G3–G4.
Word-boundary awareness under proclitics (و، ف، ب، ك، ل، ال، س) — G3–G4 in اللغة العربية. Arabic hides word boundaries inside orthographic words; this must be taught, not assumed.
الثلاثي vs فوق الثلاثي, and returning a ثلاثي to its واوي/يائي root — الصرف مضمّن at G5, matn البناء في الصرف at G6. REQUIRED for الألف اللينة; there is no other way to decide دعا vs رمى.
Recognition of أوزان الفعل (الثلاثي، الخماسي، السداسي) with their أمر and مصدر — G5 مضمّن, consolidated G6. REQUIRED for همزة الوصل والقطع.
Ranking of الحركات in strength (كسرة > ضمة > فتحة > سكون) and the ability to locate a hamza's own حركة and that of the letter before it — G5–G6 via الصرف. REQUIRED for الهمزة المتوسطة at G6.
الإعلال والإبدال — لامية الأفعال at G7. REQUIRED for الهمزة المتطرفة and for the edge cases of الألف اللينة.

Reading unvowelled text with إعراب-based vowel recovery — ملحة الإعراب at G7. REQUIRED before the G8 shift to WRITING unvowelled prose; without it the student either over-vowels everything or writes ambiguously.

classicalTexts.title: FINDING (not a text): there is no classical matn for الإملاء comparable to الآجرومية in النحو or البناء in الصرف
classicalTexts.justification: I am not aware of any transmitted متن مختصر devoted to الإملاء as a school discipline. Historically the material lived inside كتب أدب الكاتب and inside رسم المصحف literature, and the modern school subject of الإملاء was codified in the twentieth century. The Council should NOT ask for a matn here, and no one should supply one from memory. If a member knows a genuine short متن في الإملاء, it should be named and verified before adoption. Registering this absence explicitly is the honest scholarly result and protects the curriculum from an invented attribution.

classicalTexts.title: أدب الكاتب — ابن قتيبة الدينوري
classicalTexts.justification: A foundational work of the أدب الكاتب tradition addressing what the secretary/writer must command, including the discipline of the hand and correct written usage. Appropriate as a heritage anchor showing students that concern for correct writing is an old Islamic scholarly concern, not a modern school invention. NOT suitable as a student syllabus text — its organisation and lexical assumptions are far above a G10–G12 non-native reader, and its orthographic sections do not map onto the modern رسم إملائي being taught.

classicalTexts.title: المقنع في رسم مصاحف الأمصار — أبو عمرو الداني
classicalTexts.grade: G10 (وحدة: teacher reference and selected extracts)
classicalTexts.justification: The standard early authority on the ʿUthmānic rasm. It is the correct scholarly basis for the G10 وحدة distinguishing الرسم العثماني from الرسم الإملائي. Used as teacher reference plus short extracts, not as a memorised or examined text — its subject is Qur'anic orthography, which belongs to Programme 1; الإملاء borrows from it only enough to settle the editorial question of how a student writes a quoted آية.

classicalTexts.title: عقيلة أتراب القصائد في أسنى المقاصد — الإمام الشاطبي (القاسم بن فيره)
classicalTexts.justification: The versification of المقنع, a genuine and widely transmitted نظم in رسم المصحف. I am confident the work exists as named. I am NOT confident it belongs in the grade curriculum at all: it is a رسم/قراءات text whose natural home is the Ijazah track or a Programme 1 subject, and it presumes prior memorisation habits and a قراءات teacher. Recommend it be offered only to Ijazah-track candidates and only if a qualified teacher is present — never as a compulsory الإملاء item.

classicalTexts.title: قواعد الإملاء — عبد السلام محمد هارون
classicalTexts.grade: G9–G12 (student reference) and G5–G8 (teacher syllabus source)
classicalTexts.justification: A short, well-known modern manual covering exactly the rule-set this design delivers G5–G7 (الهمزة بأنواعها، الألف اللينة، التاء، الحذف والزيادة، الوصل والفصل). Modern, not classical — declared as such. Its value is that it gives the school a single fixed authority so that teachers across G5–G12 do not each teach a slightly different rule.

classicalTexts.title: الإملاء والترقيم في الكتابة العربية — عبد العليم إبراهيم
classicalTexts.grade: G8–G9 (teacher reference; source of the punctuation syllabus)
classicalTexts.justification: A standard modern reference specifically covering علامات الترقيم alongside الإملاء — the area where Arabic school practice is most inconsistent and where SHRS needs one house standard. Modern, not classical. Recommended as the source document for the G8 punctuation block and for the school-wide marking policy.

classicalTexts.title: مورد الظمآن في رسم أحرف القرآن — الخراز
classicalTexts.grade: not recommended for the grade curriculum
classicalTexts.justification: A West African–transmitted نظم in رسم and ضبط, which would be regionally apt for a Nigerian institution. I am reasonably but not fully confident of the exact title wording and of its transmission profile in this region, so I will not place it in the architecture. Flagged for the Council to verify locally with a قراءات teacher rather than adopted on my say-so.

lifecycles.prematureIntroductionRisks: Specific, not generic. (1) Teaching همزة الوصل والقطع before G5 is teaching an unmotivated exception list: the rule is decidable only from أمر الثلاثي vs الخماسي والسداسي, so without الصرف the child memorises "اسم بلا همزة" and then over-generalises to إسلام, أحمد, إبراهيم — creating errors that did not exist before the lesson. (2) Teaching الألف اللينة before the child can return a ثلاثي to its root produces pure coin-flipping between ا and ى at roughly chance level, and the wrong half gets motorically rehearsed. (3) Teaching الهمزة المتوسطة before حركة-ranking is secure converts the single most SYSTEMATIC area of Arabic orthography into the area students most fear — and fear of hamza is what makes secondary students avoid vocabulary they cannot spell, which silently shrinks their written register. (4) Formal dictation TESTS at G2–G3, as opposed to copy-and-rewrite practice, produce writing avoidance; the child who writes less gets less transcription practice, which is a closed negative loop, and it is the actual mechanism by which early spelling pressure lowers final spelling attainment. (5) At G1–G2 the non-Qur'an week is only about 7 periods; any timetable line for الإملاء would consume roughly 14% of the entire week for a skill that cannot yet be exercised. (6) Introducing the الرسم العثماني contrast early — say G4–G6 — while the child is still building a single stable orthography would be actively destabilising: he would not yet have one system firmly enough to perceive a second as a second.
lifecycles.delayRisks: Equally specific. (1) The window between the onset of free written production (G4–G5 here) and the naming of الإملاء is a window of rehearsed error. Arabic hamza and ة/ت errors laid down in that window are among the most persistent literacy faults into adulthood; correcting a fossilised spelling costs many times what teaching it correctly the first time costs. (2) Redline 7 is right but carries one real hazard, and this design exists to close it: a skill that is nobody's timetable subject easily becomes nobody's responsibility, corrected inconsistently by whichever teacher notices. The G5 named strand with an independent mark is the specific countermeasure — without it, "longitudinal" degrades into "unowned". (3) Delaying the رسم عثماني / رسم إملائي distinction past the point students quote Qur'an in writing produces graduates who write الصلوة in an ordinary essay, or — the worse error — who re-spell an آية into الرسم الإملائي inside ﴿ ﴾ and believe that is acceptable. In this school students begin quoting Qur'an in writing from G6 (التفسير العملي with English/Yoruba rendering), so G10 is already the latest defensible placement, not an early one. (4) Delay past G7 collides الإملاء with البلاغة, النقد والآداب and الإنشاء والخطابة in the secondary years, where working memory must be spent on argument and imagery, not on where the hamza sits. (5) The institution's international ambition: a graduate's application to an Arabic-medium university is read as a sample of his literacy before it is read as a sample of his فقه. Orthographic errors are the single cheapest reason for such an application to be discounted, and they are entirely preventable. (6) Nigeria-specific: delay leaves Yoruba/English romanisation habits (writing ع/ء undifferentiated, ص/س undifferentiated) uncorrected precisely during the years الترجمة begins, and cross-language interference is far easier to prevent at G6 than to unpick at G10.
lifecycles.g12Role: Not a teaching entity at G12 — a graduation threshold and an other-directed skill. Every G12 written deliverable (the بحث or رسالة قصيرة, the مقال, the script of a خطبة) is held to a published orthographic standard and returned for correction rather than silently marked down inside a content grade. Concretely, the SHRS graduate can: write extended UNVOWELLED Arabic prose with correct hamza in initial, medial and final position including the hamza+tanwīn cases; write ة / ت / ه and ا / ى correctly without hesitation; handle الوصل والفصل (مما، ألّا، لئلا، حينئذٍ); punctuate Arabic to a consistent house standard; quote Qur'an in الرسم العثماني inside ﴿ ﴾ and say WHY that differs from how he writes the same words in his own sentence; quote and takhrīj a hadith correctly; write أسماء الأعلام والكنى correctly (أبو/أبي/أبا، ابن at line-start, عمرو); normalise an older printing or a photographed manuscript into modern رسم when quoting it, and declare that he has done so; and proof-read another person's Arabic accurately. He is also, practically, aware that he has met THREE Arabic writing systems in his schooling — الرسم الإملائي, الرسم العثماني, and (if العروض is taught) الكتابة العروضية — and knows which governs which context. That three-systems awareness is something only a school like this one can give, and it is الإملاء's distinctive contribution to the graduate.
lifecycles.periodsRequested: ZERO permanent periods at every grade G1–G12. This is the headline and it is what makes redline 7 affordable and correct. Breakdown against the ceiling: G1 — nothing, 0 of the ~7-period week. G2–G3 — 0 dedicated; approximately 8–10 minutes per week taken from inside القراءة والتهجي's existing allocation (≈0.25 period-equivalent), which is affordable within a 7-period week only because it is not a new line. G4 — ≈0.25–0.5 period-equivalent inside اللغة العربية's existing allocation, 0 of the 19. G5–G7 — ≈0.5–1.0 period-equivalent per week, drawn from within the اللغة العربية / النحو والصرف allocation: one 10–15 minute قطعة إملاء with a correction-and-rewrite cycle, plus rule presentation in the closure of الصرف lessons. Still 0 new lines on the 19-period grid; this is a reallocation INSIDE an existing subject, and the subject teacher must be told explicitly that this time is protected. G8–G9 — ≈0.5 period-equivalent inside اللغة العربية / الإنشاء والخطابة, plus a cross-subject marking policy that costs 0 periods in any subject because it changes how existing written work is marked, not how much is set. G10 — the وحدة is the only place where a real block is requested: roughly 8–10 periods TOTAL, concentrated in one term (≈1 period/week for one term), taken from اللغة العربية's existing allocation and then released. It must NOT be taken from the ring-fenced 195-hour Qur'an hour unless the Council rules that رسم المصحف is a Qur'anic science and funds it there. G11–G12 — 0 dedicated periods; entirely embedded in writing the student is already doing. Cumulative permanent claim on the 19-period ceiling across twelve years: zero.
relationshipToOtherSubjects: FED BY — القراءة والتهجي (G1–G5): the direct parent. Decoding and transcription are the same knowledge run in opposite directions. This is why الإملاء is hosted here at G2–G3 rather than in اللغة العربية: the mechanics live in this strand, and it already has a separate book and independent assessment to carry the work.

FED BY — the practical التجويد / مخارج الحروف strand inside the ring-fenced Qur'an hour (G1–G12): supplies phoneme discrimination at zero timetable cost. For a Yoruba-speaking intake this is the decisive input, because ع/ء، ح/ه، ق/ك، ص/س، ض/د، ظ/ذ، ط/ت، ث/س are not contrastive in the learners' first language and an unheard phoneme is an unwritable one. Also supplies الوقف awareness, which is what makes ة/ه separable.

FED BY — حفظ القرآن (G1–G12): enormous incidental exposure to written Arabic, but a MIXED input. Daily reading of the muṣḥaf trains the eye on الرسم العثماني (الصلوة، الزكوة، الرحمن، أولئك، بأييد), which is a systematic source of predictable 'errors' in ordinary writing. This interference is unique to a Qur'an school and is the reason the G10 وحدة exists at all. At G4 the affected high-frequency words are pre-empted as a memorised list rather than fought.

FED BY — الصرف (G5 مضمّن، G6 البناء في الصرف، G7 لامية الأفعال): the engine of the entire rule-set. همزة الوصل والقطع, الألف اللينة, الهمزة المتوسطة and الهمزة المتطرفة are all صرف questions wearing orthographic clothes. The G5/G6/G7 placement of إملاء content is derived from the الصرف ladder, not chosen independently.

FED BY — النحو (G6 الآجرومية، G7 ملحة الإعراب): supplies noun/verb discrimination (needed for التاء المفتوحة) and, from G7, the إعراب that makes reading and then writing unvowelled text possible — the precondition for the G8 shift.

FEEDS — الإنشاء والخطابة (wherever placed; recommended G8+): إملاء is its non-negotiable substrate and الإنشاء is the only place إملاء can actually be proved. These two must be timetabled in the same hands or at least coordinated; if الإنشاء lands elsewhere than G8, الإملاء's assessment host moves with it.

FEEDS — الترجمة (G6+): guards the boundary in both directions. Arabic spelling must not be contaminated by English/Yoruba romanisation habits, and Arabic phonemes must not be flattened to the nearest Latin letter. G6 is the year both subjects are live, so the contrastive work belongs there.

FEEDS — الحديث، مصطلح الحديث (G10–G11)، السيرة والتاريخ الإسلامي: correct writing of أسماء الرجال والكنى, of تخريج formulas, and of quoted matn. A student who writes أبو حنيفة where أبي حنيفة is required has made a نحو error; one who writes عمر for عمرو has made an إملاء error; both are marked, but by different subjects.

FEEDS — البلاغة، النقد والآداب، أصول الفقه، أصول التفسير (secondary): all are assessed through extended Arabic writing. الإملاء's G8–G12 role is to make that writing readable without the reader spending attention on decoding it.

MUST NOT DUPLICATE — النحو and الصرف: الإملاء USES their rules and never teaches them. Diagnostic for the board: if an إملاء lesson has drifted into explaining أوزان or إعراب, it has stopped being إملاء and is stealing another subject's time.

MUST NOT DUPLICATE — التجويد: the two share مخارج الحروف as a phonetic fact, but الإملاء must never teach أحكام التجويد terminology (إظهار، إدغام، إقلاب). It takes the ear the Qur'an hour built and uses it; it does not re-teach the theory.

MUST NOT DUPLICATE — علوم القرآن / القراءات: رسم المصحف as a transmitted system belongs to Programme 1. الإملاء owns only the CONTRAST and the practical editorial ruling (which system do I use, here, in this sentence). If the Council assigns the G10 وحدة to Programme 1 instead, الإملاء should keep the editorial ruling and surrender the rest.

MUST BE COORDINATED WITH — العروض (if taught at all): الكتابة العروضية deliberately violates الرسم الإملائي (هذا written هاذا, الرحمن written أررحمان, silent letters dropped and pronounced ones added). This is a THIRD Arabic writing system. If العروض is taught without an explicit briefing that it is a notation and not a spelling, it will destabilise إملاء in exactly the students who are strongest at both.

ADJACENT AND CURRENTLY HOMELESS — الخط العربي (naskh/ruqʿah as a taught hand): legibility is distinct from orthography and does not appear in the 26-subject register as given. الإملاء cannot absorb it without becoming something else. Flagged to the Council.
departuresFromSubmission: The submission omits الإملاء from G1–G7 entirely. I accept redline 7's ruling (never a standalone timetable subject) but override the practical consequence of the omission: an unnamed skill becomes an unowned skill. I therefore name its HOST at every single grade, so that at no point in twelve years is the answer to 'whose job is this?' unclear.

I give الإملاء an INDEPENDENT MARK at G5, G6 and G7 while it remains مضمّن. The submission's implied position is that a longitudinal skill carries no separate assessment. That collapses form and assessment, which the architecture explicitly forbids. مضمّن + independently assessed is exactly the combination this discipline needs during rule delivery, and I then convert it back to embedded assessment at G8 once the rules are delivered and only application remains.

I place first meaningful appearance at G2, not G1. G1's writing work is letter formation under القراءة والتهجي; there is no orthographic choice at letter level, therefore no إملاء. I mark G1 '—' deliberately rather than writing a cosmetic مضمّن across all twelve grades for the sake of a full row.

I add a G10 وحدة on الرسم الإملائي vs الرسم العثماني, for which the submission has no provision anywhere. In an ordinary Arabic school this would be an optional refinement. In a school whose constitutional first programme is القرآن وعلومه and whose students read the muṣḥaf for 195 hours every year, it is the difference between a graduate who understands two writing systems and one who is confused by them.

I locate the G2–G3 host in القراءة والتهجي rather than in اللغة العربية, then move the host to اللغة العربية from G4. This refines rather than contradicts redline 7 — it stays inside Programme 2 and never becomes standalone — but it puts the work where the mechanics actually live, in the strand that already owns letter forms and decoding and already has a separate book and an independent mark.

I decline to add the phoneme-discrimination work to الإملاء's own cost. It is already delivered inside the ring-fenced Qur'an hour by practical التجويد. The submission does not draw this link; it is the single largest free asset this subject has, and it is specific to this institution's design.
openQuestions: [COUNCIL DECISION REQUIRED] Does SHRS teach الخط العربي (a named hand — نسخ or رقعة) at all? It is not in the 26-subject register as given to me. Handwriting legibility is a distinct competence from orthographic correctness, and at present it has no curricular home. الإملاء should not be made to absorb it by default.

[COUNCIL DECISION REQUIRED] Which programme owns the G10 وحدة on رسم المصحف — اللغة العربية (as I have provisionally placed it) or Programme 1 / علوم القرآن? My recommendation is that الإملاء hosts it because the operative question is editorial ('how do I write this in my essay'), with a قراءات-competent teacher as partner. If the Council rules it a Qur'anic science, it must still NOT be funded from the ring-fenced 195 hours without an explicit constitutional ruling.

[COUNCIL DECISION REQUIRED] Where do الإنشاء والخطابة land? الإملاء's G8–G12 assessment host and its whole application phase are built on the assumption that sustained composition begins around G8. If الإنشاء is placed earlier or later, the G8 conversion from independent to embedded assessment moves with it.

[COUNCIL DECISION REQUIRED] Is العروض taught, and at which grades? If yes, an explicit briefing that الكتابة العروضية is a notation and not a spelling is mandatory in the year it starts, or it will destabilise إملاء in the strongest students.

[COUNCIL DECISION REQUIRED] Which riwāyah and which printed muṣḥaf convention does the school use? The rasm and ḍabṭ conventions of different printings differ, and West African printings differ from the Madīnah muṣḥaf in hand and in ḍabṭ marks. This materially changes the interference profile the G4 word-list and the G10 وحدة are designed around. I will not assume an answer.

[COUNCIL DECISION REQUIRED] Does the Council know of a genuine short متن في الإملاء? I am not aware of one and will not supply a name. If none exists, the school should accept that this subject is governed by a modern house manual (قواعد الإملاء لعبد السلام هارون is my recommendation) rather than by a matn, and should say so openly rather than manufacture a classical pedigree.

[COUNCIL DECISION REQUIRED] Should the school publish a single house orthographic standard binding on ALL subjects' written work from G8? The G8–G12 design depends on it. Without a published standard, the same student is marked by five different conventions.

lifecycles.firstMeaningfulAppearance: G6 — and the accepted redline is right, for reasons the submission does not state. "Meaningful" for الترجمة means the first point at which the act of rendering can itself be taught, corrected and assessed as an act — rather than being invisible L1 glossing that happens anyway. That requires four things to already exist: automatic Arabic decoding (القراءة والتهجي, complete G5), direct comprehension of short Arabic without L1 mediation (اللغة العربية G5-G6), الإعراب sufficient to not mis-assign فاعل/مفعول (الآجرومية G6), and the concept that a text carries a meaning distinct from its words (التفسير العملي G6). All four land at G5-G6 and not before. [PROFESSIONAL INFERENCE] A critical distinction the board must hold: Yoruba/English glossing occurs in every Arabic lesson from G1 in this sociolinguistic setting. That is a teaching-medium decision, NOT the subject الترجمة, and must never be labelled as such on a timetable or a report card. Calling G1-G5 glossing "الترجمة" is the single easiest way to destroy this subject before it starts.

gradeByGrade.content: Not taught. No prerequisite exists: the child has no Arabic to render, no written English, and no metalinguistic awareness that languages differ structurally. Teacher Yoruba glossing of الحروف والمفردات happens and is legitimate as medium of instruction — it is not الترجمة and must not be recorded as such.

Not taught. Same reasoning as G1. The 7-period ceiling at G1-G2 [RECOVERED] is fully consumed by القراءة والتهجي, اللغة العربية and the embedded التوحيد/الفقه العملي; there is no period to take and nothing to teach if there were.
Not taught. The child is at الكلمات level in اللغة العربية. Any 'translation' at this stage is word-substitution, which is the exact habit the discipline later has to undo.

Not taught. [NEW ENGINEERING DECISION] Teacher-method directive only: from G4 the Arabic teacher's glossing becomes disciplined — oral, one-way (Arabic→Yoruba), never written down as a parallel text, and never presented as 'what this says in Yoruba' for Qur'anic material. This is timetable-invisible and costs nothing, but it protects G6.

Not taught. النحو والصرف are still مضمّن and الإعراب is not yet secure; a child who cannot identify فاعل from مفعول will invert agent and patient in rendering and be marked 'wrong at translation' when the fault is النحو. Introducing the subject here would misdiagnose a grammar deficit as a translation deficit.

[CURRENT COUNCIL DIRECTION, protected] Debut inside the التفسير العملي pair, sharing its separate book. Content: oral Yoruba and written English rendering of the meaning of short Qur'anic passages the child has ALREADY memorised in the Qur'an hour — never unmemorised or doctrinally contested material. The term ترجمة المعاني is taught in lesson one and printed on page one of the book; the child learns a fixed opening formula (معنى هذه الآية...) and learns that what they produce is never called القرآن باليوربا. Target: an agreed list of roughly 60 Qur'anic phrases rendered accurately in both languages. Independent assessment is on meaning-accuracy and correct framing only — never on style. It must be independently assessed at G6 precisely because an un-assessed translation strand inside a تفسير block will be quietly dropped by every teacher under period pressure.

Continues with التفسير and extends to hadith matn already learned in الحديث. Introduces the literal-vs-sense distinction by demonstration before terminology: the teacher shows a word-order-literal Yoruba rendering that produces nonsense, then the sense rendering, and only then names ترجمة حرفية / ترجمة معنوية. The student must identify, in a known hadith, one Arabic word with no single Yoruba or English equivalent and say why. Yoruba remains oral. English remains written at phrase and short-sentence level.

[NEW ENGINEERING DECISION] Partner changes from التفسير to اللغة العربية. The task changes in kind: the source is now UNSEEN non-sacred Arabic prose (a قصة, a سيرة paragraph), so the student can no longer recover meaning from memory and must actually read to render. Teaches the compulsory intermediate step — an Arabic-to-Arabic gloss of the hard word BEFORE any rendering — which is the single most effective guard against L1-mediated decoding. Teaches the no-one-to-one principle systematically. Marked for meaning accuracy only. One of the Arabic block's periods is ring-fenced as the rendering session; no marginal period requested.

Register is introduced: the same proposition as it appears in a fiqh text, a narrative, and a letter. First controlled reciprocal work (Yoruba/English→Arabic), strictly capped: single sentences in fixed frames drawn only from vocabulary the student already produces. This cap is deliberate — uncapped L1→Arabic at G9 produces calqued Arabic that fossilises. Assessment: unseen Arabic passage rendering plus a five-sentence controlled reciprocal task.

[NEW ENGINEERING DECISION] Partner changes again, to البلاغة, in its first year. This is the most productive pairing in the whole arc: البلاغة names what the Arabic is doing; الترجمة asks what survives the move. Every figure studied (مجاز، كناية، تقديم وتأخير، إيجاز) is followed by a rendering task and a written loss-note. The transliterate-only category is formalised here: terms that must be carried across as terms, not rendered — against the school's own verified Arabic–Yoruba Islamic term list. Assessment: rendering plus loss commentary. Still no marginal period; one fortnightly session inside the البلاغة allocation.

Differentiation year. The object of study stops being the text and becomes the act of rendering. Content: formal treatment of ترجمة حرفية vs ترجمة تفسيرية/معنوية from مناهل العرفان; why a rendering of the Qur'an is never itself called القرآن and what that means for public Yoruba tafsir practice in this region; audience and register as determinants of choice; the school's Arabic–Yoruba Islamic term list, including semantic drift in the Arabic-derived Yoruba Islamic lexicon; and the discipline's central exercise — placing two published renderings of the same passage side by side and judging between them on stated grounds. Assessment: comparative-judgement papers and rendering with justification. 2 periods/week — the first marginal periods this subject has ever requested.
gradeByGrade.text: مناهل العرفان في علوم القرآن (الزرقاني) — extract on ترجمة القرآن only

gradeByGrade.content: Capstone, portfolio-based. Three pieces under supervision: (1) a 600–900 word unseen Arabic prose text (fiqh, hadith commentary or tafsir register) into written English with a translator's commentary justifying every contested choice; (2) an oral Yoruba rendering of a Qur'anic passage with its تفسير, delivered and recorded, assessed on accuracy AND on correct ترجمة المعاني framing before a listening audience; (3) a short controlled English/Yoruba→Arabic piece (notice, letter, summary) marked for absence of calque. Plus an explicit ethics component: the limits of one's own competence and when the correct professional answer is 'I cannot render this — refer it.' 2 periods/week.
gradeByGrade.text: مناهل العرفان (extract) + الإتقان في علوم القرآن (السيوطي) — extract on ترجمة القرآن

lifecycles.differentiationPoint: G11 — مستقل. [NEW ENGINEERING DECISION] Why not G10: at G10 البلاغة, مصطلح الحديث (per accepted redline 1) and أصول الفقه are all newly arriving disciplines. Adding a fourth new independent subject into the 19-period ceiling in the same year is not an allocation, it is a wish. More substantively, the intellectual content that makes الترجمة a distinct discipline rather than an exercise is the analysis of what does NOT survive transfer — and that analysis is inarticulate without a year's deposit of بلاغة vocabulary. At G10 the student can feel that something was lost; at G11 the student can name it (مجاز، كناية، تقديم وتأخير، إيجاز) and argue about it. Why not G12: the defining competence — judging between two candidate renderings and defending the choice on grounds of meaning, register and audience — cannot be built and then exercised to portfolio standard inside a single terminal year. G11 gives the doctrine year and G12 gives the production year; compressing both into G12 yields a subject that is examined but not practised. Why not earlier than G10 at all: before G10 there is nothing for a standalone subject to teach that the partner subject is not teaching better with the source text in front of it.
prerequisites: Automatic Arabic decoding, so reading is not itself the obstacle — established by القراءة والتهجي, G5
Direct comprehension of short connected Arabic without L1 mediation — established by اللغة العربية, G5-G6
الإعراب sufficient to identify فاعل، مفعول، مضاف and not invert agent and patient — established by النحو / متن الآجرومية, G6
Recognition of the derivational family of a root, so an unknown word can be approached before it is rendered — established by الصرف / البناء في الصرف, G6
A productive stock of roughly 800–1000 Arabic words — established by اللغة العربية by end of G6
The concept that a text has a meaning distinct from its surface words — established by التفسير العملي, G6
Written English at sentence-and-paragraph level — comes from the MORNING national curriculum, outside this scope; must be confirmed to exist by G6 or the English direction slips
Oral Yoruba fluency — ambient from home, present at G1
Written Yoruba orthography, including tone marking and ẹ/ọ/ṣ — [UNVERIFIED] in this curriculum and possibly absent from the morning curriculum; this is why Yoruba stays ORAL until at least G10
Named figures of speech with which to describe loss — established by البلاغة, G10
Technical-register Arabic (isnād and legal vocabulary) — established by مصطلح الحديث at G10-G11 and أصول الفقه

classicalTexts.title: مناهل العرفان في علوم القرآن — محمد عبد العظيم الزرقاني
classicalTexts.grade: G11–G12 (extract only, the section on ترجمة القرآن)
classicalTexts.justification: The standard extended Arabic treatment of the question, and the clearest classical-register articulation of ترجمة حرفية vs ترجمة تفسيرية. It is the one text that gives this subject an Arabic-language doctrinal spine rather than an imported modern translation-studies vocabulary. Extract only — the full work is a علوم القرآن reference, not a translation textbook, and belongs to that subject if it is taught.

classicalTexts.title: الإتقان في علوم القرآن — جلال الدين السيوطي
classicalTexts.justification: Supplementary. Used for one comparison exercise against الزرقاني, to show the student that the question has a history and is not a modern invention. I am confident the work and its author are as named and that it addresses the translation question; I have NOT verified the exact chapter placement and the school must have a teacher confirm the passage before printing it.

classicalTexts.title: كتاب الحيوان — الجاحظ (remarks on الترجمان and the difficulty of translation)
classicalTexts.justification: The work and author are certain. Al-Jāḥiẓ's remarks on the translator and on what resists translation — particularly in poetry and religious material — are the earliest well-known Arabic reflection on the problem and would give the G12 student real intellectual pleasure. However I cannot from memory specify the volume and page or quote the passage, and I will not approximate it. Mark the extract itself as requiring verification against a printed edition before use.

classicalTexts.title: [No classical matn exists for this discipline]
classicalTexts.justification: Stated deliberately. الترجمة is not a classical Islamic science with a متن-and-شرح tradition, and the board must not go looking for one or accept a proposed one uncritically. It is a modern applied competence about which the classical tradition left discussions, not manẓūmāt. Every other subject in Programme 2 differentiates around a matn; this one correctly does not, and that asymmetry is a feature. Any text later proposed as 'the matn of الترجمة' should be treated as suspect until independently verified.

lifecycles.prematureIntroductionRisks: Four specific, not generic. (1) Entrenchment of L1-mediated decoding: a child taught before G6 that understanding Arabic MEANS producing a Yoruba equivalent builds a permanent two-step processing path. The measurable symptom appears at G8-G9 as inability to read an unseen Arabic paragraph without stopping at every content word — the exact failure that makes ملحة الإعراب and لامية الأفعال unusable as reading tools rather than memorised objects. This is the primary risk and it is not reversible cheaply. (2) Grammar deficit misdiagnosed as translation deficit: before الآجرومية (G6) the child cannot reliably assign فاعل and مفعول, so renderings invert agent and patient. Assessed as translation, the child is marked wrong at a skill they were never taught and correct at a skill they lack. (3) The Qur'an-specific hazard, which is the sharpest one here: an eight- or nine-year-old producing Yoruba renderings of āyāt without the ترجمة المعاني safeguard may come to hold the Yoruba as the thing itself. In a region where public Yoruba-language Qur'an exposition is a live and socially prominent practice, that misconception does not stay in the classroom. (4) Opportunity cost at G3-G5, where every one of the 19 periods is load-bearing for القراءة، التجويد، الآجرومية-preparation and الفقه; there is no slack, so an early الترجمة period is taken directly from a subject with a harder floor.
lifecycles.delayRisks: Also four, and they are why G6 rather than G9 is correct. (1) The habit forms whether or not it is taught. In a Yoruba/English ambient environment every Arabic lesson glosses; a student who reaches G10 untaught has already done nine years of unexamined, unmonitored translation and arrives with fossilised word-substitution habits. Forming a habit is far cheaper than replacing one, and this is the decisive argument. (2) The graduate's actual regional function goes untrained: Yoruba-language tafsir, khutbah and fatwa relay is the principal public work an Arabic-trained graduate in this region does, and if the school does not train it, it is learned by imitation from whoever is loudest — including the ترجمة المعاني framing, which is exactly the safeguard most likely to be lost in imitation. (3) The English direction is the school's international legibility. A graduate who cannot render Islamic scholarship into accurate written English cannot present the institution's work outside Nigeria, which is a stated institutional ambition, not a nicety. Deferring to G10 leaves too little runway for written English to reach portfolio standard by G12. (4) Reciprocal direction runway: L1→Arabic must start small and controlled at G9 to be safe at G12. Delay compresses it into a single year, at which point it will either be dropped or done badly.
lifecycles.g12Role: مستقل, 2 periods/week, capstone and portfolio. The graduate can, demonstrably: render an unseen classical Arabic prose passage of 600–900 words in fiqh, hadith-commentary or tafsir register into accurate written English, with a commentary defending contested choices; deliver an oral Yoruba rendering of a Qur'anic passage with its تفسير to a listening audience, correctly framed as ترجمة المعاني and never as القرآن; state and defend the choice between a literal and a sense rendering for a named text and a named audience; recognise the terms that must be transliterated rather than rendered and use the school's verified Arabic–Yoruba Islamic term list; produce a short controlled English or Yoruba→Arabic piece free of calque; and — the part that matters most professionally — recognise the boundary of their own competence and decline a text that is beyond it. What the graduate is NOT: a professional literary translator, and not someone licensed to produce a translation of the Qur'an. The G12 course says so explicitly.
lifecycles.periodsRequested: [RECOVERED ceiling respected throughout.] G1–G5: 0 periods — not taught. G6–G7: 0 marginal periods; الترجمة lives inside the التفسير العملي مدمج block, consuming roughly a quarter to a third of that block's time and sharing its book. G8–G9: 0 marginal periods; ONE period of the existing اللغة العربية (النصوص) allocation is ring-fenced as the rendering session — a claim on how an existing period is used, not a new period. G10: 0 marginal periods; one fortnightly session inside البلاغة's allocation. G11: 2 periods/week — the first and only new claim on the 19-period ceiling in the subject's entire twelve-year life. G12: 2 periods/week (one taught, one portfolio supervision). Total marginal cost across the whole ladder: 4 period-years out of a 12-year programme. This subject is affordable precisely because it spends five years as a guest of other disciplines, and the board should weigh the G11–G12 request in that light: it is the cheapest differentiating subject in Programme 2.
departuresFromSubmission: PROTECTED, not overridden: the G6 debut inside التفسير العملي (accepted redline 8) is correct and I am defending it — but for a reason the submission does not give. It is correct not because تفسير is convenient but because the regional public function of the graduate is Yoruba-language Qur'anic exposition, and that function is better taught with safeguards than absorbed without them. The submission treats the pairing as a placement; it is actually the highest-stakes translation task in the discipline and must be taught as such.

CONSTRAINT ADDED to redline 8: the term ترجمة المعاني must be taught in the first lesson of G6 and printed on page one of the shared book, and the child must learn a fixed opening formula. Source material at G6 is restricted to passages the child has already memorised in the Qur'an hour. Without these constraints the redline is a doctrinal hazard rather than a curricular decision.

OVERRIDE on modality: the submission says 'rendering to English and Yoruba' without distinguishing them. They are not symmetrical. English rendering is WRITTEN from G6 (English literacy comes from the morning curriculum). Yoruba rendering is ORAL ONLY from G6 through G9 and written only from G10 if and when written Yoruba orthography is confirmed. Teaching written Yoruba rendering to children who have never been taught Yoruba tone marking produces an unmarkable artefact and a demoralised class.
COMPLETION of the undetermined arc: the submission explicitly leaves post-G6 open. Fixed here as مدمج G6–G10 with a rotating partner, مستقل G11–G12.

OVERRIDE on partner: the submission implies التفسير as the permanent host. I rotate it — التفسير (G6–G7) → اللغة العربية/النصوص (G8–G9) → البلاغة (G10). Each rotation marks a genuine change in the task: remembered sacred text → unseen prose → analysed loss. Leaving it with التفسير for five years would leave the student able to render only what they already know, which is not translation.

NEW CONSTRAINT: the reciprocal direction (Yoruba/English→Arabic) is deliberately withheld until G9 and capped at controlled single sentences in fixed frames until G12. الترجمة must not become the school's route to Arabic composition — that belongs to الإنشاء والخطابة. Translation-led composition produces calque.

ASSESSMENT REFINED, not changed: independent assessment retained from G6 as submitted, because an unassessed strand inside a مدمج block is always the first thing dropped. But the G6–G8 rubric is restricted to meaning-accuracy and correct framing. Style, elegance and fluency are not assessed before G10 and are not assessed seriously before G11.
relationshipToOtherSubjects: FED BY القراءة والتهجي (G1–G5): decoding must be automatic before rendering is attempted. If a G6 cohort still decodes effortfully, delay الترجمة for that cohort rather than lowering the task.

FED BY اللغة العربية (G1 onward): supplies the lexical stock and, critically, the direct-comprehension method. The arrow must not reverse — الترجمة must NOT be allowed to license grammar-translation inside the Arabic lesson. The Arabic lesson stays Arabic-medium; الترجمة is where the rendering happens, and only there.

FED BY النحو (الآجرومية G6, ملحة الإعراب G7): supplies role assignment. Most 'bad translations' at G6–G8 are actually إعراب failures and should be referred back to النحو, not re-taught as translation.
FED BY الصرف (البناء في الصرف G6, لامية الأفعال G7): supplies root-family recognition, which is how an unknown word is approached before it is rendered.

FED BY التفسير (G6 onward): supplies the meaning that is to be rendered. The boundary is absolute and must be written into both schemes of work — التفسير's outcome is 'what the āyah means'; الترجمة's outcome is 'how that meaning is said in Yoruba/English, and what does not fit'. Same lesson, two traceable outcomes.
FED BY البلاغة (G10): supplies the vocabulary of loss. This is the prerequisite that determines the differentiation point.

FED BY مصطلح الحديث (G10–G11, per redline 1): supplies technical-register Arabic and, incidentally, the model of a discipline with its own controlled vocabulary — useful precedent for the G11 student.

FEEDS الإنشاء والخطابة: the graduate who can render can preach from an Arabic source in Yoruba or English. But the direction of dependence matters — الإنشاء owns Arabic composition; الترجمة borrows from it and never substitutes for it.
FEEDS الدراسات الحديثة: modern Arabic media and contemporary scholarly prose into English is a G12 application, and the two subjects should share a text bank rather than each building one.
FEEDS the institution's international function directly: Arabic→English written competence is what makes an SHRS graduate legible outside the Yoruba-speaking region.

MUST NOT DUPLICATE أصول التفسير: the hermeneutic rules for determining meaning belong there. الترجمة consumes the conclusion and does not re-derive it. If الترجمة starts adjudicating between تفسير positions, it has overstepped and should be pulled back.
MUST NOT DUPLICATE الإملاء (longitudinal within اللغة العربية, per redline 7): Arabic orthography is not a translation outcome and must not be marked as one.
MUST NOT ABSORB the Qur'an hour: the ring-fenced 195 hours [RECOVERED] are حفظ and practical تجويد. الترجمة draws on what is memorised there but takes not one minute of it, at any grade.
openQuestions: [COUNCIL DECISION REQUIRED] Does the morning national curriculum teach written Yoruba — orthography, tone marking, ẹ/ọ/ṣ? This single fact determines whether written Yoruba rendering is possible at all, and from which grade. Until answered, Yoruba stays oral through G9 and the G10–G12 written Yoruba component is provisional.

[COUNCIL DECISION REQUIRED] The school must commission, from local Yoruba-speaking scholars, a verified Arabic–Yoruba Islamic term list: which terms are carried across as terms, which are rendered, and where the established Yoruba Islamic register has drifted semantically from the Arabic. This board cannot produce that list and must not guess at it. The G10 transliterate-only teaching and the whole G11 lexicon component depend on it.

[COUNCIL DECISION REQUIRED] Confirm by what grade the morning curriculum delivers written English at paragraph level. If it is later than G6, the English direction at G6–G7 must be reduced to phrase level and the written load shifted to G8.

[COUNCIL DECISION REQUIRED] Staffing may be the real binding constraint, not the timetable. G11–G12 مستقل requires one teacher competent simultaneously in classical Arabic, written academic English, and written Yoruba. If that person does not exist on staff, the honest options are to team-teach, to run G11–G12 as دوراني in defined terms, or to defer differentiation — not to appoint someone who has two of the three.

[COUNCIL DECISION REQUIRED] Governance of Qur'an rendering exercises: does the school want a written policy on what students may and may not produce in Yoruba from Qur'anic material, and who reviews recorded G12 oral renderings before they leave the building? Given accepted redline 6's precedent of requiring protective framing for sensitive material, I judge this needs the same treatment.

[UNVERIFIED] The exact placement of the الجاحظ passage in كتاب الحيوان. Verify against a printed edition before any extract is set; do not reconstruct it from memory and do not substitute another source.

Open design question for the board: whether the G11–G12 مستقل course should carry a separate certificate endorsement, given that the الإجازة track (redline 2) is opt-in and mastery-paced and الترجمة is neither. My inclination is no — it is a normal graded subject — but the interaction is worth a ruling.

lifecycles.firstMeaningfulAppearance: G4, مضمّن inside the التوحيد والفقه block. "Meaningful" for العقيدة is not the first time a child says a creedal word — that happens at G1 in التوحيد العملي and at G3 through النشيد. It is the first point at which a learner can (a) hold a proposition about الغيب as a truth-claim distinct from a story, (b) attach a reason to it ("كيف نعرف؟ — الدليل"), and (c) retain it as a member of a named set rather than as an isolated phrase. That threshold is reached at G4 in this curriculum because two enabling conditions land simultaneously: the learner has by then accumulated a memorized Qur'anic evidence base in the ring-fenced Qur'an hour [RECOVERED] which makes "الدليل" answerable at zero period cost, and the الحديث والسيرة مدمج block at G4 has supplied narrative material about الملائكة والرسل واليوم الآخر that can now be sorted into a structure instead of merely enjoyed. Before G4, teaching العقيدة as a distinct thing produces recitable phrases, not belief-content, and double-counts what التوحيد is already doing properly. [PROFESSIONAL INFERENCE]

gradeByGrade.content: No separate existence, and correctly so. All creedal formation at G1 is التوحيد العملي مضمّن as the submission has it: Allah is الخالق الرازق، He alone is asked and thanked، محبة النبي ﷺ، through gesture, picture and daily situation (before eating, when frightened, when given something). No أركان الإيمان as a list, no taxonomy of الغيب, no negation-of-other-beliefs content. An independent عقيدة block here would also consume from the 7-period G1 ceiling [RECOVERED] that القراءة والتهجي — the true bottleneck of the whole twelve-year ladder — cannot spare.

Still no separate existence. التوحيد العملي مضمّن extends to very short sentences matching the اللغة العربية ladder: الله ربي، الله خلقني، الله يراني. The verb 'يرى' carries the whole creedal payload of the year (المراقبة) without any abstraction being demanded. Nothing here is عقيدة as a discipline; naming it so would inflate the register and force a partner allocation the 7-period ceiling cannot fund.

Creedal vocabulary does circulate at G3 — through النشيد والمحفوظات (the submitted منظومة التوحيد والإيمان) and through الحديث مضمّن — but that circulation is memorization, not instruction in العقيدة, and it belongs in النشيد's and الحديث's slots. Words arriving before their meanings is the same deliberate technique as حفظ القرآن and is legitimate; what is not legitimate is assessing it as عقيدة. I rule العقيدة '—' at G3 to keep the memorized material from being graded as doctrine a nine-year-old cannot yet hold. Note: 'منظومة التوحيد والإيمان' is not a text I can identify as a named classical منظومة — see open questions.

gradeByGrade.partner: التوحيد (inside the submitted التوحيد والفقه مدمج block)
gradeByGrade.content: FIRST MEANINGFUL APPEARANCE — and a departure from the submission, which shows no عقيدة at G4. أركان الإيمان الستة are introduced as a named set at recognition level: الملائكة (created of light, do not disobey, two named — جبريل، ميكائيل)؛ الكتب (four named, القرآن the last)؛ الرسل (names already met in السيرة والحديث)؛ اليوم الآخر (البعث، الجنة والنار asserted as reality, not as story)؛ القدر at the single sentence 'الله يعلم كل شيء وما شاء كان' with no theodicy and no جبر/اختيار. Each rukn is pegged to one short āya the child already has from the Qur'an hour. Deliberately excluded: any نفي of other beliefs, any فرق, any صفات discussion. Assessment is oral recognition inside the block — the child can name the six and give one Qur'anic peg for each.

gradeByGrade.text: نواقض الإسلام (as content only — not memorized as a list)
gradeByGrade.content: Consolidation with دليل: each rukn now carries its evidence and one consequence for behaviour. الأسماء الحسنى taught for effect, not theory (الرحيم → رجاء؛ السميع البصير → مراقبة), with no صفات method statement. نواقض الإسلام retained per redline 6 but bounded: taught strictly in the first person as ما يحفظ إيماني — not memorized as a ten-item list (a memorized list is precisely the checklist a child can misapply), not attached to named persons, groups, relatives or identifiable local practices, and with no تكفير vocabulary placed in a child's mouth.
